model_reported.name: conduire-experience-optimisation
model_reported.summary: Proposed one bounded 64-byte SSE2 grouping experiment, contrasting with prior 16-byte variants, and left official measurement to the controller.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: Kept the SIMD path guarded by the SSE2 compile-time feature macro with a scalar fallback because exact build flags are not supplied.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: The proposal uses the same guarded SSE2 intrinsics as prior valid candidates and introduces no new API or version-sensitive feature.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared recorded mean times, noted both prior SIMD variants were slower than baseline, and made no claim about this unmeasured candidate.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the prior T2 outcomes as motivation for testing a different block granularity, not as evidence that SIMD is inherently slower.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline measured 49.623 µs mean; the two prior valid T2 SIMD candidates measured 60.430 µs and 77.825 µs mean. Neither established a speedup.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 64-byte grouped scan on the official mixed-width workload and run the official ASCII and malformed-boundary checks.

proposal.hypothesis: A guarded SSE2 scan that checks four adjacent 16-byte vectors as one 64-byte ASCII superblock may amortize scan-loop overhead relative to earlier 16-byte scans on long ASCII spans. If any byte in a superblock has its high bit set, the unchanged scalar scanner finds and validates it, including stray continuation bytes. The official mixed-width n=65536 workload must determine whether larger blocks help or merely add overhead.

retained: Added a compile-time-guarded SSE2 scan that loads four 16-byte vectors only when at least 64 bytes remain, combines them to test whether the full 64-byte block is ASCII, and skips the block only when every byte is ASCII.
Retained scalar ASCII scanning, strict UTF-8 decoding, scalar tail handling, ABI, output, and thread budget.
